catapult.title: Efficient 3-Step Workflow: predict → trace → simulate
catapult.principle: The fastest path to success is: (1) predict_first_contact to confirm the red ball hits the catapult arm, (2) trace_green_ball to verify the green ball lands in the basket x AND y range, (3) simulate_action only when both checks pass. Skipping steps 1-2 wastes simulation budget on invalid placements.
catapult.when_to_apply: Always — use this as the default workflow for every new placement attempt.
catapult.example: Seed 27: predict confirmed arm contact, trace confirmed final position, then simulate succeeded on first try.

catapult.title: Verify Green Ball Reaches Basket X AND Y Range via trace_green_ball
catapult.principle: Before simulating, trace_green_ball must confirm the green ball's final resting position is within both basket x-range (≈2.8–4.5) AND basket y-range (≈-1.3 to -3.5). A green ball that reaches basket x but is at y=-0.12 or y=-4.78 will miss the blue ball entirely.
catapult.when_to_apply: After every placement change, before calling simulate_action.
catapult.example: Seed 28 step 4: green ball at (3.51, -4.78) looked promising in x but was on the floor; simulation failed.

catapult.title: Canonical Default Starting Placement: x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4
catapult.principle: When the pivot (gray_ball) is near x≈-0.93 to -1.2 and the catapult arm launches the green ball rightward, start with x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4. This placement reliably hits the arm and is valid in most standard configurations. If invalid (overlap), switch to the adaptive fallback skill.
catapult.when_to_apply: First attempt in any new catapult scene unless scene geometry indicates the arm is positioned unusually high (green_ball start y > -1.0).
catapult.example: Seed 27: x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 was valid and hit the arm, but green ball plateaued short — requires further tuning.

catapult.title: When Plateau: Try x=0.05, Not x=0.0
catapult.principle: If trace_green_ball shows the green ball's final x-position is nearly identical across multiple radius values (plateau around x≈2.5), shift the strike X from 0.65 toward 0.05 — NOT to 0.0. x=0.0 causes massive overshoot (green ball reaches y≈-0.12, far above basket); x=0.05 is the sweet spot just before the overshoot cliff. If x=0.05 still undershoots slightly, binary search between 0.03 and 0.10.
catapult.when_to_apply: When radius tuning at x≥0.3 produces identical end positions (plateau), indicating the catapult has hit an energy ceiling at that strike point.
catapult.example: Seed 27: x=0.65/0.3/0.15 all plateaued at x=2.54; x=0.0 overshot to y=-0.12; x=0.05 gave end=(4.04,-1.34) and succeeded.

catapult.title: Adaptive Fallback When Default y=0.0 Invalid: Raise to y=2.5, Use x=-0.3
catapult.principle: If x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 is invalid due to object overlap, raise the drop height to y=2.5 to clear the arm. At y=2.5, use x=-0.3 with r=1.4 as the primary fallback — this reliably hits the arm and sends the green ball into the basket region. At elevated y, changing radius can flip the launch direction entirely (e.g., r=1.0 launches left, r=1.4 launches right), so prefer x-shifting over radius tuning.
catapult.when_to_apply: When canonical y=0.0 placement is blocked by arm overlap; also when radius tuning at y=2.5 switches launch direction.
catapult.example: Seed 29: y=0.0 invalid; y=2.5, x=-0.3, r=1.4 gave end=(3.73,-2.71) and succeeded.

catapult.title: Incremental Radius Tuning as First Response to Short Landing
catapult.principle: If trace_green_ball shows the green ball ends short of the basket (x < 2.8), first try increasing radius by +0.2 (e.g., 1.4 → 1.6) before shifting x. More mass transfers more momentum to the catapult arm. Only shift x if two consecutive radius increases produce nearly identical end positions (plateau).
catapult.when_to_apply: When the green ball is directionally correct (heading right) but undershooting in x.
catapult.example: Seed 27 step 3: r=1.4 gave x=2.54, tried r=1.6 — same plateau, then correctly shifted x.

catapult.title: Elevated Arm Scene: Use x=1.1, y≈1.0, r=2.0
catapult.principle: When the green ball starts significantly higher than usual (start y > -1.0, indicating the arm is elevated), conventional placements (x=0.65, y=0.0) often fail or produce leftward launches. Strike the far-right end of the arm with x=1.1, r=2.0, and drop height y≈1.0–1.1. The large radius compensates for the arm's elevated position and delivers sufficient energy for a rightward launch into the basket.
catapult.when_to_apply: After checking get_level_state and finding green_ball start position y > -1.0 (arm resting higher than normal).
catapult.example: Seed 28: green_ball start at (-2.88, -0.57); x=1.1, y=1.05, r=2.0 gave end=(4.36,-2.87) and succeeded.

catapult.title: Drop Height Y is a Precise Energy Lever Near Sharp Cliffs
catapult.principle: Near the catapult energy threshold, the drop height y acts as a fine-grained energy control: a 0.05 change in y can shift the green ball's final x by over 1 unit. When a placement is close but the green ball lands slightly short or long, tune y in increments of 0.02–0.05 rather than large jumps. The direction to tune: lower y = less energy = shorter range; higher y = more energy = longer range.
catapult.when_to_apply: After identifying a placement (x, r) that produces a promising but imprecise trajectory, and radius tuning has already been exhausted.
catapult.example: Seed 28: x=1.1, r=2.0; y=1.0 gave end=(3.27,-1.66); y=1.05 gave end=(4.36,-2.87) — 0.05Δy changed final x by >1 unit.

catapult.title: Use get_level_state When All Default Placements Are Invalid
catapult.principle: If canonical and fallback placements are all rejected as invalid, call get_level_state to read actual object positions before continuing. The arm position, green ball start height, and basket location vary across seeds. Scene geometry information is necessary to choose a valid and effective placement rather than guessing blindly.
catapult.when_to_apply: After 2+ consecutive invalid placement rejections, especially when standard x/y coordinates fail.
catapult.example: Seed 29 step 2: all defaults invalid; get_level_state revealed arm at y=-1.36 spanning x=-3.27 to 0.98, explaining the overlap.

catapult.description: Agent persists with catapult strikes for many steps without verifying that the green ball ever reaches basket HEIGHT (y≈-1.3 to -3.1) during its arc — not just basket x-range.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents fixate on the x-coordinate as the success metric and treat any rightward trajectory as progress, ignoring that the ball must also be at basket depth.
catapult.how_to_avoid: After every trace, check BOTH end_x in [2.8, 4.5] AND end_y in [-1.3, -3.5]. If end_y is outside this range, the trajectory is wrong regardless of x.

catapult.description: Agent fine-tunes radius (or y-height) at a fixed position when the catapult exhibits a sharp threshold cliff — tiny Δr or Δy causes swing from 'too short' to 'overshoot to floor'.
catapult.why_it_happens: The catapult's mechanical advantage creates non-linear energy transfer; small parameter changes near the pivot angle threshold produce wildly different outcomes.
catapult.how_to_avoid: When two consecutive radius/height values bracket a large output swing, use binary search with 0.02–0.05 step sizes. Alternatively, shift x to find a more stable operating region.

catapult.description: Agent attempts placements in the basket/ledge region (x≈2.5–3.5, y≈-1.5 to -2.5) as deflectors that are consistently INVALID due to object overlap.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents try to create a deflection path when the direct catapult approach seems to be failing, but the basket and ledge objects fill this space.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Never attempt x > 2.0 placements as deflectors. If the catapult approach is failing, adjust the strike point or energy rather than adding deflectors.

catapult.description: Agent jumps directly from plateau at x≥0.3 to x=0.0, causing massive overshoot (green ball lands at y≈-0.12 or far above basket).
catapult.why_it_happens: The old skill recommended x=0.0 as the next step after plateau, but x=0.0 sits just past an extremely sharp energy cliff, causing dramatic overshoot.
catapult.how_to_avoid: When plateau is detected at x≥0.15, try x=0.05 first (not x=0.0). If x=0.05 overshoots, binary search between 0.05 and 0.15 in 0.03-step increments.

catapult.description: Agent attempts to knock the blue ball leftward to meet the green ball without establishing where the green ball will be when blue arrives.
catapult.why_it_happens: When the green ball consistently undershoots, agents try to meet it halfway, but without trace data on the green ball's resting position the geometry is unknown.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Always trace_green_ball first to find its resting position, then determine whether a deflector approach is geometrically feasible before attempting it.
